As we head into the summer holidays, we encourage all pupils to keep their skills sharp by continuing to practise on Times Tables Rock Stars and Sumdog. Just a few minutes each day can make a big difference—and who knows, you could be our next competition champion!
Well done once again to everyone involved, and keep rocking those times tables over the summer!

A flying start
Give your child a flying start in our caring, happy home-from-home environment led by our nurturing Early Years expert team.
At Copthorne Prep, we provide so much more than just day care. We’re Early Years experts ready to support you and your children on the exciting journey ahead. Whether it’s building self-confidence, nurturing creativity or boosting early numeracy and literacy, our dedicated staff are here to build bright futures by providing the best beginnings.
Children thrive when they feel secure, valued and celebrated by those entrusted with their care. Our approach is family friendly, supporting children and parents through vital development milestones. We work in partnership with parents, providing support, advice and the very best care, so you and your child can enjoy every step.
We are open throughout the year (48 weeks with provision from 8.00am to 6.00pm) supporting working families. Families can choose the level of support they need whether it’s five full days a week down to a minimum of two mornings a week for younger children (2 year olds turning 3) or three mornings a week for older children (3 year olds turning 4). Like standard day nurseries we accept childcare vouchers and Government funded childcare (15 hours), from the age of 3.
We provide a home from home setting with the additional expertise and benefits that come from being part of Copthorne Prep and the award winning Caterham School family.
The Early Years are when lifelong foundations are laid, and magical memories are made. Visit us and find out how our Flying Start nursery can help your child thrive.

ISI Inspection
Our most recent ISI inspection was in January 2026 with a report that reflects not just a successful school, but a thriving, joyful community.
We have a consistently strong track record in inspections, which reflects our commitment to providing a first class, transformative education for our children.
To see excellence in action, please visit us at an upcoming visitor event.
ISI Inspection 2026
Our most recent ISI inspection report (January 2026) met approval across all areas – from leadership and teaching, to safeguarding, wellbeing, curriculum and early years.
What comes through most strongly is that Copthorne is a place where children feel safe, valued, inspired and able to achieve their full potential. The inspectors repeatedly noted the warmth of relationships, the respect shown between pupils and staff, and the inclusive culture that allows every child to flourish. They recognised the clarity of our aims and values, and how fully these are lived each day – something that only happens when a whole community is pulling in the same direction.

Our people
The people that teach, support, inspire and care for our pupils are the heartbeat of our school.
They are here to guide, nurture and encourage every step of the pupil journey from Nursery through to moving on to senior school at Year 6.
Senior leadership team
Mrs Kylie McGregor
Head of School
Kylie brings a wealth of experience and expertise from a career spent in the region’s leading preparatory schools. Kylie is responsible for the day to day running of Copthorne Prep School.
Kylie joined the leadership team at Copthorne Prep School in 2022 as the Head of Pre-Prep and Nursery. Kylie has been instrumental in enhancing the nursery, driving curriculum development, and strengthening whole-school pastoral care. As the school’s longstanding Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL) Kylie ensures the highest standards of care and protection for every child.
Kylie’s previous roles include seven years as Head of Lower School at Pennthorpe School where she made significant contributions to the school’s curriculum whilst also shaping a creative, skills-based learning approach and developing an outdoor learning curriculum. During her tenure Kylie established Pennthorpe’s Pre-Prep department which gained recognition as finalist for Pre-Prep School of the Year
An advocate for nurturing future educators, Kylie mentors trainee and new teachers, working closely with the University of Buckingham to support teacher training.
Kylie graduated from the University of Brighton with a degree in Primary Education and an Early Years specialism, before beginning her teaching career in the state sector prior to a move to the independent sector.
Mr Ali Raja
Deputy Head, DSL
Ali joined the leadership at Copthorne Prep in 2025 from The Hawthorns School where he was Head of Middle School and DSL. Previous role include Head of Junior School Sport and Head of Year at City of London Freemen’s. Ali’s experience in working with Prep age children places him in the perfect role to support the older Copthorne Prep pupils.
Ms Nicola Stone
Head of Academic Excellence
Mr Ben Purkiss
Executive Head
Ben is Executive Head of Copthorne Prep School focusing on the strategic direction of the school and its overall educational, co-curricular and wellbeing provision. The responsibility of the school’s day to day running remains with the Head of School.
Ben was appointed Headmaster of Caterham Prep School in 2019 and has led the transformation of the prep school which was named as finalist for Best Independent Prep School, in the Times Educational Supplement’s 2024 Awards, the only school across Surrey, Sussex and Kent to reach this position.
Ben has a strong track record of having worked in leadership roles in some of the top performing prep schools in the south east. Prior to joining Caterham, Ben was Deputy Head at Bede’s Preparatory School in charge of the day to day running of the school with responsibility for pastoral care. He was previously Director of Studies and Head of Science at The New Beacon School in Sevenoaks and Head of Science at Copthorne Prep School. He begun his teaching career at Cottesmore Prep School having completed a degree in Physics.
Governors
Mrs. A. Fletcher
Anne is a highly experienced Early Years childcare professional and was the Manager of the Ide Hill Pre-School for some 14 years.
She joined Ide Hill C E Primary School as a Governor in October 2009 with the key focus on Early Years and Transitions. She was appointed Chair of Governors in 2012.
Three of her children attended Caterham School and during that time she was the Chair of the Parents’ Association for three years. Anne is a longstanding member of the Caterham School Foundation and Copthorne Education Committee.
Anne can be contacted via email: chairofgovs@copthorneprep.co.uk
Mr. P. Clarke
Member of the Copthorne Board of Governors and the Finance & General Purposes Committee
In his Executive career, Phil Clarke spent over 30 years in Finance and developed experience across Strategy Development and Execution, managing high growth businesses and as a leader of I.T., Logistics and Supply Chain, Procurement, Property and Procurement. He held Board level roles of CFO at Selfridges, CFO at Ann Summers and Chief Operating Officer at The White Company. His Non-Executive and Business advisory experience includes as a Non-Executive Director and Trustee of Riverford Organic Vegetables, Non-Executive Director at The Institute of Physics Publishing and Co-opted Trustee at De Montford University. Phil has also worked as Business advisor to several businesses in Retail and Recruitment.
Mrs. D. Grimason
Member of the Copthorne Board of Governors, Child Protection and Safeguarding Committee and Chair of the Finance & General Purposes Committee
Deborah was brought up in Northern Ireland and was educated in Dungannon High School for Girls Grammar and is a Solicitor of the Supreme Court and a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Secretaries. Deborah studied English Literature and Philosophy (B.A. Hons) and undertook a conversation law degree and solicitors finals at Christleton Hall Law School. After qualifying in 1987, Deborah has worked as a lawyer mostly in international industry roles, but also in private practice in London. She is currently General Counsel and Company Secretary to the Board of Ceres Power, a UK – based engineering and technology solutions provider, developing clean energy to address climate change and improve air quality.
Mr. O. Byrne
Member of the Copthorne Board of Governors, and Chair of the Welfare, Child Protection and Safeguarding Committee
Oliver is an Old Caterhamian and a practising solicitor. After leaving Caterham he studied Politics (B.A. Hons) at the University of Warwick and undertook his legal studies at Nottingham Law School. After qualifying in 2007, he worked for a number of years for various City law firms before moving to in-house legal roles.
He is currently General Counsel and Chief Compliance Officer of Trident Energy, an exploration and production company with a focus on emerging markets.
Mrs. P. Jubraj
Member of Copthorne Board of the Governors and the Finance and General Purposes Committee
Preya studied Business & Computing (BSc) at Aston University and then went on to pursue a career in the Financial Services sector with her graduate position starting out at Accenture as a Management Consultant and supported a number of clients primarily within the Insurance space. Preya had a varied and successful 17 year tenure at Accenture before moving over to Baringa where Preya continues to build on her relationships in the Financial Services sector.

School history & tradition
Founded in 1902 by the brother of the then Head of Winchester College, Copthorne Prep began its life as a small boys’ prep school feeding into Winchester College.
Now a thriving co-ed prep school feeding a range of senior schools, its original motto ‘Pervincet Vivida Virtus’ (Lively manliness conquers all) is no longer relevant, although lively minds remain a feature of Copthorne today.
Our history timeline
1897
Emsworth House, the building now known as Copthorne Prep School, became a temporary home for Twyford School whilst their own buildings were reconstructed.
1902
Copthorne Prep founded by Mr Bernard H Rendall (brother of the then Head of Winchester) as a boys’ school and feeder school for Winchester. There were just 9 boys initially.
1910
Part of the original building (initially used as an observatory, complete with tower) was converted into a Chapel, dedicated by the Bishop of Lewes.
1913
The sad news of the tragedy in the Antarctic touched many at the school as Dr Edward Wilson, Mr Bernard Rendall’s brother-in-law, had made the school his headquarters for a short time after the ‘Discovery’ Expedition. The stained-glass window funded in his honour remains a fitting tribute.
1919
The chapel tower was raised to install a clock and chimes ‘to look out over the school for the generations to come’ in honour of the twenty old boys and masters lost in WWI. A bronze plate positioned on the south side of the chapel listed the fallen.
1928
Mr Ernest Skeete Workman took over the running of the school in partnership with Mr John Philip Howard.
1939
The Rendall Memorial Library was opened.
WWII – the school was evacuated to the Lee Bay Hotel in Ilfracombe, returning in March 1945. The school building was requisitioned for use by the army.
1949
Mr Pinney, an old boy of the school replaces Mr Howard.
1952
Mr P J H Workman (Tim) took over as headmaster on his father’s death; at the age of just 25 he was at the time the youngest headmaster in the IAPS.
1963
Mr David Sale who had joined the teaching staff at the school in 1954 become joint Headmaster with Mr P J H Workman.
The Jubilee Cup competition was revived with boys competing for one of four houses, Red, Blue, Green and Silver, over a range of events. The magnificent trophy, first presented in the school’s Jubilee year, is still competed for today although the four houses now bear the names of previous Headmasters – Rendall, Workman, Sale and Newton.
1976
The school was formed into a charitable trust run by a governing body. Mr P J H Workman retired and Mr David Sale was joint headmaster with Mr David Cann (1976-1982) and then with Mr David Newton. The ‘Friends of Copthorne’ was also established.
1979
The School became co-educational.
1984
Mr David Newton became the sole headmaster.
1999
Mr Charles Allen was appointed as Head.
2002
The school celebrated its centenary with a ball at Effingham Park Hotel and a series of events at the school.
2005
Mr Chris Jones was appointed as the 8th Headmaster since being founded in 1902.
2022
Mr Chris Jones retired and leadership of the school was then handed to Mr Nathan Close, previously his deputy.
2024
Copthorne becomes part of the Caterham Family of Schools.

pageCache.text:
Journey to starting school
Joining a school, particularly if it is your child’s first school, can sometimes feel a little daunting. We hope this step by step summary helps to explain what happens at each stage of the journey.
Our Registrar, Kathryn Billingham-West will be happy to assist you with any aspect of joining Copthorne Prep and can be contacted at admissions@copthorneprep.co.uk or by telephone on 01342 859954.
Our main points of entry are Nursery, Reception and Year 3. For 8+, 9+, 10+ entry with a through offer to Caterham School, please contact the admissions team directly.
Entry points
Children can begin their education with us from age 2 in our Flying Start Nursery and continue through to Year 6 before moving on to senior school. Whilst the most common entry points are Nursery, Reception and Year 3, we welcome applications into any year group subject to places being available.
If you are considering joining the school further up the school, you can apply for 8+, 9+ 10+ entry with a through school offer to Caterham School for Year 7.
Whilst we are part of the Caterham School Family, we prepare pupils for admissions and scholarships for a range of senior schools.
Visit us
Join at one or more of our visitor events, whether it is a Saturday themed family visitor morning, a working visitor morning or a virtual visitor evening . You can also book a private tour with the Headmaster.
Visiting us more than once really helps to get a wider insight into everything we do to make your child’s time at school a happy and transformative one.
Application
Once you have visited and would like to move forward with us, register for a place by completing the application form. The application and payment will be acknowledged to you via email and our Admissions Registrar will be in touch to make arrangements for a taster session.
Taster sessions
Nursery
All children applying to join Nursery are encouraged to join our Little Caterpillars Toddler Group for at least one session. This group is a great opportunity to meet our staff and other families looking to join the Nursery. You will be invited to book in an initial settling in session with your child. This involves time with one of our Nursery Practitioners to learn more about your child to help them settle swiftly and happily into nursery life. At this session, you will have the opportunity to fully explore the nursery with your child and book a further settling in session for you to drop and leave your child for a morning of activity with the other nursery children including lunch.
Reception
Your child will be invited to attend a morning taster session with our Pre-school class where they will join their peers to take part in play based activities which could include music, PE, swimming or languages. Your child can be collected after a well earned lunch with their new friends. At this stage we would seek an informal reference from their current nursery setting (if applicable).
Years 1 to 3
Children applying for places higher up the school will be invited to attend a morning taster session with their peers in a classroom setting. As well as fun practical sessions, they will take literacy and numeracy assessments. At this stage we would also seek a reference from your child’s current setting.
Years 4 to 6
If you are applying for 8+, 9+ or 10+ entry for your child with a through offer to Caterham School, they will be invited to attend a morning taster session with their peers in a classroom setting. As well as fun practical sessions, they will take literacy and numeracy assessments and may also take verbal and non verbal reasoning tests. At this stage we would also seek a reference from your child’s current setting.
Formal offer
As soon as possible following a successful taster session, a formal offer will be made. Letters are emailed directly to parents.
Acceptance
Acceptance of an offered place is made by completing our Acceptance Form via our admissions portal together with submitting the Acceptance deposit. Following receipt of the deposit and completed form, the place is confirmed to you by email.
Once a place has been accepted, you will be invited to a number of welcome events where you will be able to find out more about starting school along with meeting other new and existing Copthorne families. Joining forms and all information relating to starting school in September is sent at the start of the Summer Term.
If you are joining the Nursery, you will be contacted to arrange a start date as soon as possible for your chosen days.
First day of School
Children starting School in September will be invited to visit the School in the Summer Term, prior to joining. They will have the opportunity to see their new classroom, meet their class teacher and get to know their peers.

Boosting early learning
Early childhood is the vital foundation on which everything is built – all that play and creativity is serious business!
Our Early Years experts ensure a secure and happy environment where important life skills such as curiosity, creativity, persistence, imagination, confidence and resourcefulness can fully develop.
Our Flying Start curriculum offers children crucial unpressurised time to gradually get ready for school life ahead; time for them to develop as individuals, form friendships, make sense of their world in their own unique ways and develop their natural creativity and love of learning.
Our curriculum is based on the Early Years Foundation stage and benefits from specialist teachers in key areas, including literacy, maths, games, music, expressive art and languages. We focus on the three prime areas that are particularly crucial for igniting children’s curiosity and enthusiasm for learning, and for building their capacity to learn, form relationships and thrive:
Our staff to child ratios of 1:5 for 2 -3 year olds, and 1:8 for 3-4 year olds, give a boost to early numeracy and literacy skills and confidence. Above and beyond the Early Years Foundation stage curriculum, we give the children a huge variety of extra experiences and opportunities. There’s something for everyone with lessons in music and dance, French language skills, water confidence and swimming in our pool, football and outdoor learning.
We incorporate digital literacy and problem-solving skills into every day. Tools like Bee-Bots and similar educational robots offer hands-on learning experiences that promote engagement, exploration, collaboration, future skills preparation, and introduce basic coding concepts.
Emily loves every minute of her time at the nursery; she never settled at her last nursery, but she never wants to leave here!

pageCache.pageTitle: Outstanding Music Exam Success - Copthorne Prep
pageCache.text:
There is a wonderful atmosphere of celebration in the Music Department this week as pupils from Copthorne Prep achieved an exceptional set of results in their recent Associated Board of the Royal Schools of Music (ABRSM) examinations.
From our youngest instrumentalists taking their first graded assessments to our more experienced musicians tackling the higher grades, pupils demonstrated remarkable dedication, musicality and resilience. Their success reflects months of careful preparation, countless hours of practice and the confidence to perform under exam conditions. The quality of the performances made a particularly strong impression on the visiting examiner, who praised not only the pupils’ musical abilities but also their professionalism, preparation and positive attitude throughout the examination day. In feedback to the Music Department, the examiner remarked that the pupils were “a real credit to the school”—a wonderful endorsement of the values, commitment and enthusiasm they bring to their music-making.
Every candidate from Copthorne Prep who took an ABRSM graded examination this term at Caterham achieved either a Merit or Distinction, highlighting the breadth of musical talent within the school.
ABRSM examinations assess far more than polished performances. Pupils are challenged in technical skills, musicianship, sight-reading and aural awareness, providing a comprehensive measure of their musical development while encouraging confidence, discipline and creativity.
These outstanding results are a testament not only to the hard work of our pupils, but also to the expertise and encouragement of our dedicated Visiting Music Teachers, whose commitment inspires pupils to achieve their very best.
We warmly congratulate every candidate who entered an examination this session. Congratulations to all involved on a truly outstanding set of results.
Congratulations to all of our pupils who have successfully completed music examinations during 2026.
Congratulations to every pupil on their hard work, commitment and musical achievements throughout the year. We look forward to celebrating many more musical successes in the future.

Curriculum
At Copthorne Prep we strive to develop confidence, provide opportunity and realise potential in every child.
This mission statement, together with our core values, underpins our curriculum. We strive to offer children the opportunity to realise their potential across the entire spectrum of academic, artistic and physical disciplines which makes up our curriculum, and we recognise that confidence and high self-esteem are essential for a successful and happy learning experience.
Our school curriculum is designed from the ground up – that is to say it begins with the early years foundation stage in the nursery and continues, through the pre-prep and prep school, offering a comprehensive and integrated syllabus along the eleven year journey.
At all times we seek to combine the very best traditions and values of a prep school education with the themes and principles of a twenty-first century curriculum, so that our children may take an active part in the modern world.
English
Using Power of Reading teaching sequences, your child will read a wide range of thought-provoking texts, incorporating fiction and non-fiction books from a variety of cultures.
Cross-curricular links with art, history, science, geography, PSHE and even DT ensure your child is inspired to read. Even the most unenthusiastic readers are motivated by the instant feedback from taking the comprehension quizzes on the popular accelerated reading scheme. We also have our very own reading therapy support dog, Pixel, who encourages a love of reading in our more reluctant readers, as well as those with a passion for books.
Our English curriculum aims to accelerate your child’s confidence, encouraging them to become thoughtful and empathetic readers and writers. With literacy at the heart of our curriculum, our whole school spelling programme helps all pupils develop spelling strategies that are then applied throughout their school career and beyond.
Mathematics
The study of maths is not simply about learning numbers and their application – it is so much more. Through studying maths, your child will develop creative thinking skills and learn to question and deepen their understanding of the practical world around them.
By making maths relevant to everyday life and supporting your child’s progress in an encouraging and positive way, they can gain a strong sense of achievement and a genuine enthusiasm for learning. Who knows where that curiosity and confidence might take them?
Science
Science is part of our everyday lives from turning on a kettle to watching a rainbow. We harness your child’s wonder at the natural world and their enthusiasm for finding out how things work to teach this varied and fascinating subject that forms part of our Global curriculum.
We focus on allowing children to experiment and follow their own ideas, creating their own investigations through a series of fun and informative practical and theory sessions.
Science is taught as a core subject. Your child will have around five science lessons a week, taught in two purpose-built laboratories from Year 3 upwards. Small classes mean your child can maximise their potential and find their strengths, building on these as they work co-operatively in practical sessions.
By encouraging your child to explore their health and environment, and share what they have learned at home, your child will continuously develop their curiosity. Budding engineers and scientists can join our after-school STEM club, using their digital and maths skills to make anything from water wheels to crystal gardens.
Geography
As well as aiding the development of non-fiction reading skills, such as maps and data, Geography helps your child to discover and make sense of the world. From comparing and contrasting different environments in the early years, through topic-based learning in the pre-prep to a stand-alone humanity subject throughout the prep school, as part of the Global curriculum, Geography:
History
Your child will explore History through the Global curriculum, learning how to form arguments and opinions on different people, events and periods in history through discussion and debate.
Our history curriculum provides a coherent knowledge and understanding of Britain’s past as well as an opportunity to examine the development of other civilisations and cultures. It aims to inspire your child’s curiosity, to help them think critically, ask perceptive questions, weigh-up evidence and examine different perspectives to make reasoned and informed judgements.
History is narratives, and we study the people, actions, decisions, interactions and behaviours that have shaped the world in which we live. We inspire a love for the past through lively and engaging teaching including traditional historical enquiry; role-play; visits to places of historical interest; and plenty of thought-provoking discussions.
Your child will leave the school as an able and confident historian, equipped with the necessary skills and confidence to analyse increasingly complex themes at senior school.
Digital and Innovation
Alongside our existing weekly curriculum provision in one of our three suites, we have introduced a UK-leading digital and innovation curriculum, pioneered by Caterham, called EDGE. It starts in Reception and continues through school. EDGE promotes problem solving and critical thinking whilst building your child’s digital skills for their education here and at senior school, university and beyond.
Languages
Language learning should not be just an activity where the ultimate goal is to achieve an academic standard that will hang on a wall gathering dust, never to be used again. It is a creative and collaborative life skill that opens doors to different cultures and experiences.
We believe that language learning should be an experience that will be remembered and treasured for the rest of your child’s life. To achieve this, we run language days, theatre visits and cultural workshops such as flamenco dancing. We want your child to leave us with a high level of language and grammar and a zest for learning.
Most pupils learn Spanish and French. In the pre-prep, French is taught by specialist teachers from Reception through to Year 2. Spanish is taught as an after-school club by a native speaker.
From Year 3 Spanish and French are taught within the curriculum. We focus on speaking and listening in Year 3, moving to a greater emphasis on reading and writing in Year 4.
Art
As part of Global, Art is a unique form of expression, building your child’s powers of analysis, observation, articulation, imagination and the ability to formulate ideas.
Art and design provides your child with a creative outlet and a visual and tactile understanding of the world and issues around them. By experimenting with different media and exploring their ideas, your child will begin to develop skills and opinions, and create a personal response. By investigating the work of others, they gain an understanding into the lives of the artists, and also into different times and cultures.
We have a light and spacious art room with separate storage areas and kiln room. Your child will have opportunities to develop their skills through drawing, painting, printmaking, clay/ceramics, photography, sculpture, textiles, 3D, colour, pattern, tone, line, shape, space, texture and form. We hold a biennial arts week, where the children are taken off timetable and take part in workshops for the entire week, working with visiting artists and holding their own art exhibition.
Drama
Drama is hugely beneficial to your child’s self-esteem, confidence and communication skills. Whether preparing for a school play, writing a sketch or participating in an educational drama lesson, your child will be actively engaged in developing the kind of life skills that will enable them to become confident, expressive and creative citizens.
At the start of your child’s educational adventure, drama is predominantly performance based, and from Year 3 it is timetabled weekly. This enables us to promote educational drama alongside performance drama; the former is taught as part of a syllabus during drama lessons; the latter is encouraged school productions, from smaller festival plays and recitals in the theatre, to whole-school musicals in the gym and weekly dramatised assemblies in chapel.
Each year your child will be able to take part in a dramatic performance. Recent productions include Shakespeare Rocks, Matilda, Alice in Wonderland, Studio Drama, Oliver, Fantastic Mr Fox, The Wizard of Oz and The Lion King.
Your child can also take LAMDA lessons from Reception onwards.
Music
Music is integral to school life and plays an important part in your child’s development. It is a unique and inspiring way of communicating, and a vehicle for personal expression. Learning music enables your child to better understand the world they live in. A creative and enjoyable activity, and an demanding academic subject, music can also help your child feel part of a community.
In addition to the weekly classroom music lessons in which children listen to, create and perform music, we encourage your child to sing in chapel and hymn practice each week. Your child can have instrumental tuition from the visiting peripatetic music teachers and take part in formal and informal concerts. We encourage your child to engage in music, whatever their ability, because an active and enriching musical experience contributes to a well-balanced and enjoyable school curriculum.
Design and technology
Our DT projects focus on developing practical skills, essential for everyday life, in a fun and exciting way using a variety of materials.
Design and technology allows children of all capabilities to design and construct ‘something’ for ‘somebody’ for ‘some purpose’. It won’t always be a great success, sometimes it may even be a great disaster, but we can guarantee it will be great fun and provide a useful learning experience.
As your child progresses through the school they will use more of our well-equipped DT room, enabling them to combine their design and making skills with knowledge and understanding to create quality products through a variety of medium and techniques, e.g. woodwork, metal work and 3D printing.
Food Tech
From Year 5 your child can partake in regular Food Tech lessons, as part of the Global curriculum, covering safe food storage, preparation, and handling. This develops an important life skill that will equip your child with a better understanding of food and food preparation. Your child will develop recipes for a range of sweet and savoury dishes, helping them to understand the principles of simple nutrition and healthy eating. Learning about nutrition and how to prepare healthy meals can prevent later medical problems such as diabetes, heart disease and obesity. Your child will learn to handle food and equipment and become aware of where their food comes from, food sustainability and religious and cultural issues that affect different diets.
Religious Studies
Religious studies plays a critical part in your child’s spiritual, moral, social and cultural development. Exploring their own beliefs and values, and developing positive attitudes to those of others, requires understanding, knowledge and skills.
Through RS your child will learn.
Self-awareness
Respect for all
Open mindedness
Appreciation and wonder
Physical Education
Physical education (PE) helps your child develop control, co-ordination and mastery of their body through movement. The thought and effort required leads to improved performance, personal achievement, understanding and increased knowledge. Your child will gain real satisfaction and enjoyment from working with a sense of purpose and practising hard, and long, enough to overcome initial challenges.
Every week your child will have an hour each of swimming and PE tuition from specialist teachers. This helps your child develop:
During PE lessons alongside fitness work, we do Badminton, Basketball, Gymnastics, Cross Country and Tennis.
A range of psycho-motor skills
Physical mobility and flexibility
Stamina and strength
Self-esteem through acquiring physical competence and poise
Self-confidence through understanding capabilities and limitations
Outdoor Learning
Outdoor learning is an integral part of our curriculum, offering dynamic, hands-on experiences that promote resilience, leadership, and collaboration. Through nature-based activities, pupils develop essential life skills while enhancing their physical and mental wellbeing and allowing them to ‘be children’. Our carefully designed sessions spark curiosity, ignite creativity, and encourage a deep respect for the environment, helping children grow into confident, well-rounded learners connected to the natural world.
Come and experience for yourself what makes a Copthorne education unique.
We would love to welcome you our School at an upcoming visitor morning or private tour.

Global curriculum
Ensuring that our pupils have the skills and knowledge to thrive in a fast-changing world, alongside a first class academic education, is one of our core priorities.
Our Global curriculum adopts an enquiry led approach to learning so that our pupils can explore and apply knowledge and skills in context to real life situations, giving them a better understanding of their place in the world.
Our Global Curriculum Pathway takes children from as early as Nursery through to Year 6. By adopting an enquiry led approach, that integrates traditional subjects such as science, humanities, art and DT, two modern European languages and music into cohesive interrelated topics, children can explore and apply knowledge and skills effectively across various contexts.
This interdisciplinary curriculum is focused on a central question each term, which allows children to foster a deeper understanding by making links and connections within the chosen topic. Our Global curriculum encourages natural curiosity, a problem-solving mindset, and builds confidence with the aim to develop well-rounded, inquisitive learners equipped to navigate an ever-changing world.
The curriculum also provides opportunities for children to learn and develop their research, planning and presentation skills, culminating in a final Year 6 project IPQ qualification which is assessed externally by the ISEB.
Our Global termly question can range from our Year 4s deep diving into ‘Is space the final frontier?’ whilst Year 1 children are exploring ‘What makes a hero super?’. Further up the school, the Global themes can encompass philosophical questions such as, ‘Why do we have wars?’ or ‘What makes a great leader?’, encouraging pupils to develop critical thinking, empathy, debate skills, ethical reasoning, and a deeper understanding of historical, cultural and social contexts.

pageCache.pageTitle: Transition to senior school - Copthorne Prep
pageCache.text:
Transition to senior school
As part of the Caterham Family of Schools, pupils in Year 5 benefit from early offers to Caterham School. The Early Offer pathway at Copthorne Prep strengthens and smooths the transition for pupils who would thrive at Caterham School.
This removes the hurdle of the 11+ entry exam, with offers awarded in the Summer Term of Year 5. These offers are based on our close understanding of each child’s strengths and potential as members of the Caterham Family of Schools. This pathway gives families the certainty of knowing their child’s secondary school destination by the end of Year 5. It also allows children to fully engage in the outstanding education at Copthorne Prep during Year 6.
As part of the Early Offer pathway, families will be invited to register for scholarship applications. Scholarship decisions will be based on both assessments at Caterham School and insights from Copthorne Prep. Assessments for scholarships will take place at Caterham School in the summer term of Year 5 and are available for Academic, Art, Chess, Choral, Dance, Drama, Music, Innovation & Entrepreneurship, and Sport. This year we are proud that 6 offers and 5 scholarships were awarded for September entry to Caterham.
Caterham celebrated record 2025 exam results. Read all about them in Achieving Full Potential
As a leading local prep school, we also support applications to a wide range of secondary schools and families benefit from thorough and expert guidance discussion about the best future school options for your child.

Wraparound care
We understand the challenges of juggling parenting and work. Our wraparound care gives you the flexibility of an extended day – from 7.30am to 6.00pm.
You can manage your diary knowing that your child is safe, supervised and having a lovely time with friends.
Early morning:
Pupils may arrive from 7.30am where they will be supervised by members of the staffing team before being directed to their classrooms at 8:00am.
Nursery & Pre-Prep after school activities:
Once school finishes at 3.30pm our after-school care starts and runs until 6.00pm.
We will escort your child to one of our activities, which typically last an hour and vary from term to term. If not participating in an activity, your child joins supervised outdoor play, weather dependant.
Should you choose, your child can stay in wraparound care and join tea at 5.20pm.
Prep school after school activities:
We run a range of after school activities which your child can join at 4.35pm when the school day ends. These last about 40 minutes. Many are run by members of the teaching staff although a few require specialist coaches. As your child gets older, they may prefer to use this time for homework which avoids having to work at home later in the day.

pageCache.pageTitle: A Fantastic Year in Art - Copthorne Prep
pageCache.text:
As the school year draws to a close and the children prepare to take their artwork home, it has been a pleasure to reflect on what a fantastic year it has been in the Art Room. Each piece reflects not only the finished result, but the curiosity, effort and enjoyment shown along the way.
Throughout the year, pupils have embraced new techniques and materials with enthusiasm. From experimenting with colour to learning new processes, they have approached every project with creativity and growing confidence.
A particular highlight has been our clay work, which proved a firm favourite. From pinch pots to decorative tiles and the more ambitious slab-built pots, the children demonstrated patience and skill. Seeing their excitement as their finished pieces emerged from the kiln was a real highlight.
Most importantly, the Art Room has been full of energy, imagination and fun. Pupils have shared ideas, supported one another and taken pride in their work.
Well done to all our young artists—I look forward to seeing what they create next.
